minutes.headline: Select Board adopted a single tax rate and approved the Electric Avenue solar PILOT agreement.
minutes.summary: The board held its annual tax classification hearing and adopted a single tax rate for all classes. It approved a solar PILOT agreement for 190 Electric Avenue after debate over the pilot versus the depreciation model, and issued a common victualler license to a new gas station and market. It also reviewed the special town meeting, the old primary school survey, FY21 budget priorities and a public Q&A before the budget, and a draft public comment policy.

what_happened.line: The Select Board adopted a single tax rate for all classes for FY2020, pending state Department of Revenue approval; the vote was unanimous.
The board accepted the solar PILOT agreement for 190 Electric Avenue in final form, with one abstention, after comparing it with a depreciation model.
The board compared ten years of depreciation payments with twenty years of PILOT payments and heard that the PILOT yields more over time.
A motion on the common victualler license for a gas station and market at 400 Electric Avenue was made, but the recording does not make the outcome audible.
The board accepted the social media policy with the change to "town manager", and agreed to hold a public question session after the January budget presentation.

why_it_matters: A single tax rate means homes and businesses are taxed at the same rate per thousand dollars of value, so the commercial and industrial classes do not carry a higher rate than residential property.
The PILOT sets fixed payments from a solar facility over twenty years in place of taxes on its equipment as it depreciates, which changes how much that property contributes to the tax base.
The January budget presentation and the planned public question session are where residents can ask about FY21 spending before the budget goes to Town Meeting.
watch_next: December 3rd workshop on the old primary school, which is also to take up the public comment policy; no meeting Thanksgiving week.
The date of the public question session after the town manager's January budget presentation, to be set by the chair and town manager.
